candidates.reason: Defines the two HTTP download-handler timeout tests that are currently disabled by an inline guard `if reactor_pytest == "asyncio" and sys.platform == "win32": pytest.skip("This test produces DirtyReactorAggregateError on Windows with asyncio")` (blocks at lines 363-370 and 381-388; each block carries a `# https://twistedmatrix.com/trac/ticket/10279` comment between the guard and the `pytest.skip(...)` call). These are the only `DirtyReactorAggregateError` comment sites in the download-handler suite besides the FTP test, so re-enabling the tests behind those comments means removing these guards here. Note: TestHttpBase is an ABC, so these two tests are actually collected and run through the concrete subclasses in tests/test_downloader_handler_httpx.py, tests/test_downloader_handler_twisted_http11.py and tests/test_downloader_handler_twisted_http2.py; those modules are unchanged by the skip removal but are the execution entry points for the re-enabled tests.

Contains the third and last `DirtyReactorAggregateError` comment in the repository: `TestFTP.test_invalid_credentials` starts with `if reactor_pytest == "asyncio" and sys.platform == "win32": pytest.skip("This test produces DirtyReactorAggregateError on Windows with asyncio")` (lines 176-180). It is a concrete FTP download-handler test (not an inherited base-class test), and `sys` is imported in this module only for this guard, so removing the guard touches this file alone.
